summary.title: [Share Rail] Facebook and LinkedIn omit the legacy document title
summary.one_line_description: All 15 floating-share routes send the display or Open Graph title instead of the full legacy document title to Facebook and LinkedIn.

bug_1.file_locations: - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/components/SocialShareRail.astro - share URL construction, Lines 7-14 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/components/ArticleEnding.astro - shared title propagation, Lines 24-46 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/layouts/ArticleLayout.astro - article ending call, Lines 21-67 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/layouts/LongformLayout.astro - long-form ending call, Lines 20-45 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/tests/e2e/ui-parity.spec.ts - share-payload expectation, Lines 640-657 and 676-696 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/js/scl.min.js - authoritative legacy share-payload construction, Lines 1-5

issue_description.description: The legacy share script deliberately uses two title sources: the Twitter payload uses the Twitter or Open Graph title, while Facebook and LinkedIn use `document.title`. `SocialShareRail.astro` accepts one `title` value and uses it for all three services. A direct comparison of the audited legacy files with the final distribution found that Twitter matches on every rail-enabled route, but Facebook and LinkedIn fail on all 15 routes. For example, `/blog/australian-health-star-rating` sends `Australian Health Star Ratings: A Failed Experiment` instead of `Australian Health Star Ratings: A Failed Experiment | Muscle Hacking`. `/supplements/` sends `Beyond the Hype: Supplements That Work` instead of `The Best Muscle Building Supplement Stack (Based on Research) | Muscle Hacking`. The E2E test passes because it derives the expected Facebook and LinkedIn title from the same H1 or `shareTitle` value used by the new component, rather than from the legacy document title.
issue_description.expected_vs_actual: | Aspect | Expected | Actual | |--------|----------|--------| | **Twitter** | Legacy social or Open Graph title plus canonical URL | Matches on all 15 rail-enabled routes | | **Facebook title** | Exact legacy document title | H1 or route-specific social title | | **LinkedIn title** | Exact legacy document title | H1 or route-specific social title | | **Coverage** | Compare each service against its legacy source field | Test uses one new-component title for all services | | **Recommendation** | Pass separate social and document titles and derive fixture expectations from the legacy metadata | One shared title hides cross-route payload drift |

summary.title: [Migration] Content extraction removes seven legacy image captions
summary.one_line_description: Rerunning the checked-in article migration overwrites seven captioned entries without their `imageCaption` frontmatter.

bug_2.file_locations: - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/scripts/migrate-legacy-content.mjs - frontmatter extraction and overwrite, Lines 74-86 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/content.config.ts - optional image-caption schema, Lines 5-20 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/layouts/ArticleLayout.astro - caption rendering, Lines 21 and 50-51 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/content/blog/australian-health-star-rating.md - retained `imageCaption` frontmatter, Line 11 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/content/blog/best-protein-powder-for-building-muscle.md - retained `imageCaption` frontmatter, Line 12 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/content/blog/healthy-low-calorie-foods.md - retained `imageCaption` frontmatter, Line 12 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/content/blog/healthy-organic-post.md - retained `imageCaption` frontmatter, Line 11 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/content/blog/normal.md - retained `imageCaption` frontmatter, Line 12 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/content/blog/reject-modernity-embrace-masculinity.md - retained `imageCaption` frontmatter, Line 12 - /Users/sacino/musclehacking/src/content/blog/what-is-intermittent-fasting.md - retained `imageCaption` frontmatter, Line 12

issue_description.description: The legacy sources contain a `.figurecap` immediately after the hero on seven articles, and the current Markdown correctly stores those values in `imageCaption`. The migration script extracts the hero image, alternative text, dimensions, and byline, but it never extracts the caption before it overwrites every Markdown file. An in-memory execution of the exact migration algorithm produced byte-identical output for only five of twelve entries. The other seven outputs were smaller and lacked only the manually retained caption frontmatter. If a maintainer follows the repository migration utility again, `ArticleLayout.astro` receives `undefined` and removes those seven visible captions from the final routes. Current `verify:dist` passes because it checks the already-correct checked-in content and does not execute or compare the migration result.
issue_description.expected_vs_actual: | Aspect | Expected | Actual | |--------|----------|--------| | **Repeatability** | Rerunning extraction preserves the current twelve article contracts | Seven generated Markdown files differ from the checked-in versions | | **Visible content** | All seven legacy hero captions remain present | `imageCaption` is removed and the caption no longer renders | | **Current verification** | A migration-result fixture rejects destructive extraction drift | `verify:dist` examines only current checked-in content | | **Recommendation** | Extract `.figurecap` into frontmatter and add a non-destructive repeatability fixture for all twelve outputs | Caption preservation depends on manual post-migration edits |
